## Chart Trajectory Over Time

The scatter plot below displays every single weekly appearance by Drake on the Billboard Hot 100 between 2009 and 2021 (2,569 individual points). Each point represents a track's position during a specific chart week, colored by whether Drake was the lead artist or a featured collaborator.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.8
#| dpi: 300

library(tidyverse)

drake_data <- read_csv("data/drake_billboard.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> 
  mutate(
    role = if_else(str_starts(performer, "Drake"), "Lead Artist", "Featured Artist")
  )

ggplot(drake_data, aes(x = week_date, y = week_position, color = role)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.42, size = 1.9) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "loess", span = 0.32, linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = c(1, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Lead Artist" = "#1e40af", "Featured Artist" = "#ea580c")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "Drake on the Billboard Hot 100 (2009–2021)",
    subtitle = "Tracking 2,569 weekly positions across lead and featured tracks",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Billboard Hot 100 Rank (1 is top)",
    color = "Drake's Role",
    caption = "Source: TidyTuesday / Billboard.com (2,569 observations)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#0f172a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#475569", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#f1f5f9")
  )
```

## Key Findings

1. **Volume and Consistency:** Across 2,569 chart entries, Drake maintained an unbroken presence on the Hot 100 spanning more than a decade (2009–2021).
2. **Lead vs. Feature Dynamics:** Early in his career (2009–2012), guest features (such as with Lil Wayne and Nicki Minaj) accelerated his exposure. By 2015–2018, Drake's lead tracks dominated the upper echelon of the chart.
3. **Chart Saturation:** Major album release weeks (such as *Scorpion* in 2018 and *Views* in 2016) placed dozens of tracks simultaneously on the chart.
